denoising_autoencoder.summary: Corrupts each bar's features and learns to rebuild the clean row; the bottleneck is the representation.
denoising_autoencoder.implementationNote: Bridge: the pretext trains on every finite bar of the training span, labels unread; a linear probe on the frozen embedding gives P(up), a Huber head the price, both early-stopped on validation. Differs from the spec: a feature row, not an image; corruption zeroes cells and adds Gaussian noise, and zeroed cells weigh more in the error. Expect: near a plain logistic regression on the same features.

pretext_epochs.label: Pretext epochs
pretext_epochs.description: Passes over the training span's unlabelled bars with the self-supervised objective; no label is read.

head_epochs.label: Probe epochs
head_epochs.description: Epochs of the linear probe on the frozen embedding (25 full-batch steps each), stopped early on the validation rows.

patience.label: Patience
patience.description: Probe epochs without a better validation loss before the probe stops.

weight_decay.label: Weight decay
weight_decay.description: Shrinks the encoder's weights toward zero each pretext step.

batch_size.label: Batch size
batch_size.description: Bars per pretext step, drawn at random from the span (contrastive methods use the rest of the batch as negatives).

embedding_size.label: Embedding size
embedding_size.description: How many numbers describe each bar; the probe reads these.

hidden_size.label: Hidden size
hidden_size.description: Units in each hidden layer of the encoder.

mask_fraction.label: Mask fraction
mask_fraction.description: Share of a row's cells set to zero before encoding.

noise_standard_deviation.label: Noise standard deviation
noise_standard_deviation.description: Gaussian noise added to every standardised cell before encoding.

corruption_emphasis.label: Corruption emphasis
corruption_emphasis.description: Extra weight of a zeroed cell in the reconstruction error (0 = all cells equal).

native.produces: A compressed code for each input row, taken from the bottleneck of an encoder that was trained to rebuild the clean row from a deliberately damaged copy, together with the rebuilt row itself.
native.targetVariable: the clean, uncorrupted feature values of the same row that was fed in damaged; no future price and no label is involved
native.objectiveNote: The denoising version damages the input first (added Gaussian noise, cells set to zero, or cells flipped to random values) and still scores the rebuild against the clean row, so copying the input straight through no longer wins and the bottleneck has to learn how the features move together.

metrics.why: The whole claim of a denoising autoencoder is that its bottleneck code is a better description of a bar than the raw features, so the test is one linear readout fitted on the code against the same readout fitted on the raw row and on the same encoder before any denoising step was taken.
metrics.baseline: the same linear readout on the raw standardised feature row, and on the same encoder left at its random starting weights

metrics.why: This is the quantity the encoder and decoder were actually trained on, measured on rows they never saw: damage an unseen row the same way, rebuild it, and ask what share of the features' variance the rebuild still misses.
metrics.baseline: rebuilding every feature with its training-span mean, which misses all of the variance, and handing back the damaged row unchanged, which misses exactly the damage that was added

metrics.why: A straight-line readout of the bottleneck code should rank bars that went up above bars that went down; it is kept secondary here because the engine's number is this readout's own score and belongs to the as-run layer for a stand-in model.
metrics.baseline: one half, the value of an ordering that has nothing to do with the outcome

metrics.why: A bottleneck that squeezes every bar onto a handful of directions can still rebuild smooth features well, so the count of directions the code really uses on unseen rows shows whether the compression kept variety or threw it away.
metrics.baseline: the embedding size, which a code spreading its variance evenly over every dimension would reach

metrics.why: The weighted squared rebuild error per pretext epoch shows whether the denoising fit settled; it says nothing about direction, and in the runnable version the same line turns into the readout's loss once the encoder is frozen.

notApplicable.name: Wasserstein Distance
notApplicable.why: It compares generated rows with real rows, and a denoising autoencoder generates nothing; it only repairs a damaged copy of a real row.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: It needs simulated price trajectories, and this model produces a code and a rebuilt feature row, never a trajectory.

notApplicable.name: Latent KL Divergence
notApplicable.why: The divergence against a Gaussian prior is the variational autoencoder's penalty; the denoising bottleneck has no prior to diverge from.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: Even coverage of a sphere is what a contrastive loss asks for; nothing in the corrupt-and-rebuild objective asks the code to be uniform.

notApplicable.name: Latent Kullback-Leibler Divergence
notApplicable.why: That term belongs to a variational autoencoder, whose code is pulled toward a prior; the denoising bottleneck is a plain deterministic code with no prior and no such penalty.

notApplicable.name: Expected calibration error
notApplicable.why: Natively there is no probability at all; the only probability appears when a class-balanced readout is bolted on, and that readout is centred on one half by construction.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: The encoder never takes a position; any trading result belongs to the readout and the engine's trading rule, which is the as-run layer.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter trains the denoising encoder and decoder on single feature rows of the fold's training span with labels unread (cells are zeroed at mask_fraction, Gaussian noise of noise_standard_deviation is added, and zeroed cells weigh more in the squared error through corruption_emphasis), then freezes the encoder and fits a class-balanced linear readout on the bottleneck code; every as-run number therefore measures the denoising code plus that straight-line readout, not the rebuild quality the specification describes.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the logistic curve applied to a single linear layer reading the frozen bottleneck code, standardised with training-row statistics; the layer starts at zero and is fitted by full-batch Adam on a logistic loss in which up rows and down rows each carry half the weight.

stepQuantity.unit: nats during the readout epochs; during the pretext epochs before them the training line holds the weighted squared rebuild error in squared standardised feature units and there is no validation value

meaningful.why: The readout on the bottleneck code was fitted with up bars and down bars each carrying half the loss, so the score that weighs the two classes the same way is the one that grades the probabilities on the scale they were trained for; the natural logarithm of two is what a readout that learned nothing scores.

It asks whether a straight line through the denoising code ranks up bars above down bars, which does not depend on the class weighting or on where the readout's probabilities are centred, so it is the cleanest test of what the code carries.

A bounded proper score of the readout's probability of up on test bars; because the readout is centred on one half instead of the fold's up share, part of it reflects that shift and not the bottleneck code.

The unweighted version is the quantity that picked the readout's epoch on validation rows, so on test bars it shows how that choice carried over, but it charges the class-balanced readout for not sitting on the base rate and is never the headline.

The bin-free slope shows whether the readout's log-odds are stretched too far or too little after early stopping on a small validation span; it is read without the intercept, which the class weighting shifts by design.
A linear readout of a noise-trained code often barely leaves one half; the spread of its probabilities shows whether the code gave the readout anything to commit on.

The share of test bars where the readout's call matched the direction, cut at one half of a class-balanced probability, so the cut sits at the even prior and not at this fold's up share; it is read against the majority-class accuracy.

It averages the hit rate on up bars and on down bars, which matches the way the readout on the denoising code was weighted during fitting, so it is the fairest of the hard-call numbers for this model.
One symmetric number for the readout's hard calls over all four confusion cells, which exposes a readout that drifts to calling nearly every bar the same way after the encoder is frozen.

It is what the readout's long-or-short call on the denoising code earned after costs under the engine's rule of following the latest call; only the side of one half the probability falls on reaches this number.
It sets the readout's trading result against simply holding the same contract over the same folds, the only same-series reference that tells apart a code with direction in it from a rising tape.
Per-bar net result of the readout's calls over its own variability; zero is an arithmetic marker and not a no-skill line, because a readout calling at random still pays costs on every flip.
The deepest fall of the equity built from the readout's calls; it describes the path that the engine's always-in-the-market rule produced from this code, not anything the encoder optimised.
Winners over losers among the trades the readout's call flips created; a readout hovering near one half flips often, so this is read with the trade count beside it.
The share of closed trades that ended positive after costs when positions follow the readout on the denoising code; it says how often, not how much, and is read with the average win and loss.
The share of bars the readout called up; a class-balanced readout should sit near the middle, so a share close to all or none means the frozen code moved between training and test bars.
The count of trades is the count of call flips, stops, targets and fold ends; for a readout whose probability hugs one half it shows how much of the result is cost from flipping.

It grades a second fit of the same adapter, whose linear head on the denoising code was trained with a Huber loss on the scaled horizon move, against forecasting no move on the same bars; it tests the code's information about size and sign together.
The average miss in points of the Huber head on the denoising code, tick-rounded before scoring, read beside the miss of forecasting no move on the same bars.
How often the sign of the Huber head's forecast matched the move on bars where both are non-zero after tick rounding; it comes from the second fit, not from the readout whose call is traded.
The size of the gradient before clipping during the corrupt-and-rebuild epochs shows whether the encoder and decoder trained smoothly; the readout epochs report none.

The search over the pretext learning rate and mask_fraction is scored by the trading objective on inner blocks of the training span, so it is an optimistic selection score for this model and never a result.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The readout is class-balanced, so its probabilities are centred on one half and not on the up share the bins are compared with; the gap is built in.
The same built-in shift toward one half decides the worst bin, and with probabilities this close together few bins are occupied.
It measures the gap to the observed up share in each bin, which the class-balanced readout is offset from by construction.
The class weighting sets the readout's average near one half whatever the tape did, so the mean says nothing about a lean in the denoising code.
The training line holds the class-weighted loss with a weight penalty and the validation line the unweighted loss, so their difference is not an overfit gap.
With the default dials the engine is always long or short once the readout has made a call, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not this model.

caveats: The training line switches quantity at the first readout epoch: before it the line is the weighted squared rebuild error of the denoising pretext, after it the class-weighted logistic loss of the readout, and validation values exist only after the switch.
The price forecast comes from a second fit of the same adapter, with its own denoising pretext run and a Huber head; it is not the model whose call is traded.
The pretext reads every finite bar of the training span, labelled or not, and no validation or test bar; the readout's epoch is chosen on validation rows, so validation numbers are optimistic.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks several bars ahead, so any interval around these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than MNQ the cost per side is the MNQ account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

self_distillation.summary: A student network matches a slowly moving copy of itself (the teacher) across several augmented views of the same bar.
self_distillation.implementationNote: Bridge: the pretext trains on every finite bar of the training span, labels unread; a linear probe on the frozen embedding gives P(up), a Huber head the price, both early-stopped on validation. Differs from the spec: views are jitter, scaling and feature dropout of a row; the student matches the EMA teacher's output and hidden layer; a variance hinge prevents collapse. Expect: near a plain logistic regression on the same features.

projector_size.description: Width of the projection head the pretext loss reads (dropped for the probe).

off_diagonal_weight.label: Off-diagonal weight
off_diagonal_weight.description: Weight of the redundancy term (squared off-diagonal cross-correlations).

native.produces: An embedding vector for each input from the shared backbone, with the projection head discarded after pretraining; the method outputs no direction, probability or price.
native.targetVariable: The cross-correlation matrix between the projections of two distorted copies of the same batch of inputs, which training pushes toward the identity matrix; the future price move is never read.
native.objectiveNote: This version of the pretext loss has two parts: the diagonal of the cross-correlation matrix is pulled to one so each embedding dimension agrees across the two views, and the off-diagonal entries are pulled to zero, weighted by off_diagonal_weight, so no two dimensions repeat each other; it needs neither negative examples nor a second network.

metrics.why: The published test of a redundancy-reduction encoder is to freeze the backbone and fit one straight-line classifier on it, so how well that classifier orders unseen bars is the method's own grade; it is also what the Model Cycle measures, because the runnable model is that same readout.
metrics.baseline: The same straight-line classifier fitted on the raw feature row of the same series, and one half as the value of a ranking unrelated to the outcome.

metrics.why: Decorrelating the embedding dimensions is only worth the training time if a readout on them beats the identical readout on the raw feature row and on the backbone at its random starting weights, which is the comparison this number makes.
metrics.baseline: The identical linear readout on the raw feature row and on this backbone with its starting weights, same folds and same series.

metrics.why: The off-diagonal term only removes straight-line correlation between embedding dimensions inside a training batch, so measuring how much the dimensions still tell about one another on unseen rows checks whether the redundancy really went away; decorrelation is weaker than independence, so this is a check and not a promise of the method.

If the diagonal term loses to the off-diagonal term, some embedding dimensions go flat and the batch standardisation divides by almost nothing; the count of directions the embedding really uses on unseen rows shows how many dimensions stayed alive.
metrics.baseline: The embedding width set by embedding_size.

metrics.why: The cross-correlation loss is estimated on each batch, so its curve is noisy at small batch sizes and says only that the matrix is nearing the identity on training rows; it has no validation counterpart, and in the runnable model the logged curve changes to the readout's loss once the backbone is frozen.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test on a price series measures the data, not an encoder trained on the cross-correlation of two views.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: It is a fractional-differencing quantity; the twin encoder differences nothing and keeps no series memory.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: The twin encoder produces a continuous embedding and never a cluster label, so there is no grouping to score.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: The embedding dimensions are standardised and decorrelated, not ranked by variance; the effective rank and the independence check replace it.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction Residual
notApplicable.why: The model has no decoder; its loss compares two projections and never the input row with a rebuilt copy.

notApplicable.name: Expected calibration error
notApplicable.why: Natively there is no probability at all, and the readout added to run it is class-balanced, so its output is centred on one half rather than on the series' up share.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable model trains the redundancy-reduction encoder on single feature rows of the fold's training span with labels unread, using scaling, feature dropout and jitter as the two views in place of the specification's time warping and masking, and estimates the cross-correlation matrix on each batch; it then freezes the encoder and fits a class-balanced straight-line readout for the probability of up. Every as-run number therefore measures the frozen embedding plus that readout, not the cross-correlation loss. The cross-correlation objective is only the encoder phase: the probability that is traded and scored comes from the readout, which is fitted by a class-weighted logistic loss, so that loss is the objective the run optimises for its output.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the logistic function of one linear layer on the frozen encoder's embedding, taken before the projection head and standardised with the training rows' statistics; the layer starts at zero and is fitted by full-batch Adam on a logistic loss in which up bars and down bars each carry half the weight, and no calibration map is applied afterwards.

stepQuantity.unit: the cross-correlation loss on its own unitless scale during the pretext epochs, then nats per bar of class-balanced logistic loss during the readout epochs

meaningful.why: The readout on the decorrelated embedding was fitted with up bars and down bars each carrying half the loss, so the score that weighs the two classes equally on test bars matches what the readout was asked to do; its reference is the natural logarithm of two, the value of quoting one half on every bar.

It asks whether the embedding whose dimensions were made to agree across views and not repeat each other, read through one linear layer, puts up bars above down bars, whatever the centring of the class-balanced readout.

A bounded proper score of the readout's probability on test bars; the class-balanced readout pays a small fixed price whenever the series' up share is away from one half, which belongs to the readout and not to the twin encoder.

The unweighted score of the readout's probability on test bars; it is the quantity the readout's kept epoch was chosen on over validation bars, so the validation value is optimistic and only the test value is a fair reading.

native.objectiveNote: This model's puzzle is self-distillation, a cross-entropy between a student and an exponential-moving-average teacher with no negative pairs, and the vision transformer it was designed for is reduced to one dimension here, so a patch is a run of consecutive bars and not a square of pixels.

metrics.why: The self-distillation puzzle never sees a direction, so the literature judges the teacher transformer's class token by freezing it and asking whether a single linear layer on it can order up bars above down bars; this is the same number the Model Cycle reports for this model, so the native and the as-run primary are one quantity.
metrics.baseline: One half, the value of an ordering that carries no information, which is a mathematical constant.

metrics.why: It asks what the student-teacher training added by fitting the identical linear layer on the raw window features and on the same patch transformer before any distillation step, on the same folds.
metrics.baseline: The same linear layer on this model's raw input window and on its untrained transformer, on the same folds.

metrics.why: If teacher centring and temperature sharpening fall out of balance every window lands on one prototype or on all prototypes equally, the distillation loss still looks fine, and only a count of how many independent directions the class token uses on unseen windows reveals it.

It describes whether the transformer's heads concentrate on a few patches of bars or spread evenly over the window, which is the emergent property this method is known for and an explanation aid only.
The student-to-teacher cross-entropy by epoch shows only that the student kept tracking a moving teacher; a low value is also what a collapsed teacher produces, so it is never read as quality.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes an input price series, while this model outputs a feature vector per window and makes no claim about stationarity.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: This ratio belongs to fractional differencing of a price series; the student and teacher transformers difference nothing and keep no such memory parameter.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: The prototype scores are a training device that is thrown away after pretraining, and the model never assigns bars to groups whose tightness could be graded.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: Explained variance grades a linear projection that rebuilds its input, and this transformer has no decoder and keeps no ordered components.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction Residual
notApplicable.why: Nothing is reconstructed: the student is trained to match the teacher's prototype distribution, not to rebuild the bars it was shown.

notApplicable.name: Held-out reconstruction error
notApplicable.why: The masked patches are scored against the teacher's prototype scores for those patches and never rebuilt as bar features, so there is no rebuilt input to compare with the real one.

notApplicable.name: Expected calibration error
notApplicable.why: The embedding states no odds, and the linear layer used to read it is fitted with each class carrying half the loss, so its output sits around one half whatever the series' own up share is.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: The pretraining takes no position and reads no price outcome, so any trading figure belongs to the readout and the engine's trading rule and not to the representation.

stepQuantity.unit: nats, with the pretext epochs holding the student-to-teacher cross-entropy and the probe epochs holding the class-weighted logistic loss

meaningful.why: The linear layer on the teacher's class token was fitted with each class carrying half the loss, so this score, which weights up bars and down bars equally, is the proper score on the scale that readout was aiming at; its reference is the natural logarithm of two, the score of always saying one half.

It tests whether the self-distilled class token carries any ordering of up bars over down bars that one linear layer can read, independent of where the class weights centred the probability; it coincides with the native primary.
A bounded second look at the linear readout's probabilities on the teacher's class token, read with the knowledge that they are centred on one half and not on the fold's up share.

The hard call cuts the readout's probability at one half, the point the class weights centred it on, so averaging the hit rate over up bars and down bars is the fair count of calls for this teacher embedding.
One symmetric number for the up or down calls read from the teacher's class token, which stays near zero if the linear layer learned to call a single side.

The share of correct calls from the linear readout on the class token, to be read beside the majority-class accuracy of the same fold because the readout's cut reflects its even prior and not the series' up share.
It shows without bins whether the linear layer on the teacher embedding spreads its probabilities too widely or too narrowly, which early stopping on few validation rows can cause.

It is what the sign of the linear readout on the teacher's class token earned after costs when the engine went long at one half or above and short below, so it tests the direction call and nothing about the size of the probability.

The same direction calls from the readout on the self-distilled embedding per unit of bar-to-bar swing in profit, under the engine's rule and costs; zero is an arithmetic marker and not a no-skill reference because a random caller pays costs.
The deepest fall of the account while following the readout's direction calls on the teacher embedding, which describes the path of those calls under the engine's rule.
Winning trade dollars over losing trade dollars for trades opened and closed by flips of the linear readout on the class token, after costs.
The share of closed trades that made money, where a trade lasts until the readout on the teacher's class token flips side or the fold ends, so it reflects flips and not single predictions.
How often the linear readout on the class token calls up, shown beside every trading number because a readout stuck on one side simply holds the market.

The forecast line comes from a second fit of the same adapter, a separately pretrained teacher transformer with a linear Huber layer on its class token, so this tests that second embedding against forecasting no move on the same bars.
The typical miss in points of the Huber layer on the second teacher embedding, to be read against the no-change forecast's miss on the same bars.

The share of forecasts from the Huber layer on the second teacher embedding whose sign matched the move, counted only where both are non-zero after tick rounding; it is a different model from the one whose calls are traded.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The readout was told by its class weights to centre on one half, so the unweighted score charges it for the gap between that even prior and the fold's up share and not for what the teacher embedding knows.
Calibration against the observed up share is biased by construction for a readout whose class weights centre it on one half.

The training curve holds the student-to-teacher cross-entropy and then a class-weighted logistic loss, while the validation curve holds the unweighted logarithmic loss, so their difference compares different quantities.
With long-only off and no stop or target the engine is always in the market once the readout has made a call, so this number describes the engine's rule.

The price forecast is a second, separately pretrained copy of the model with a Huber layer, so the forecast line and the traded call do not come from one embedding.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks label_horizon_bars ahead, so any interval around these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

weight_decay.label: Weight decay
weight_decay.description: Shrinks the encoder's weights toward zero each pretext step.

batch_size.label: Batch size
batch_size.description: Bars per pretext step, drawn at random from the span (contrastive methods use the rest of the batch as negatives).

embedding_size.label: Embedding size
embedding_size.description: How many numbers describe each bar; the probe reads these.

hidden_size.label: Hidden size
hidden_size.description: Units in each hidden layer of the encoder.

jitter_strength.label: Jitter strength
jitter_strength.description: Standard deviation of the noise added to every standardised feature of a view.

scaling_strength.label: Scaling strength
scaling_strength.description: Standard deviation of the random factor each feature of a view is multiplied by.

feature_dropout.label: Feature dropout
feature_dropout.description: Share of a view's features set to zero, a different set per bar.

projector_size.label: Projector size
projector_size.description: Width of the projection head the pretext loss reads (dropped for the probe).

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.description: Softmax temperature of the contrastive (or prototype) scores; lower is sharper.

prototype_count.label: Prototype count
prototype_count.description: Learned cluster centres the bars are assigned to.

sinkhorn_smoothing.label: Sinkhorn smoothing
sinkhorn_smoothing.description: Entropy smoothing of the equal-share assignment; smaller is closer to hard.

sinkhorn_iterations.label: Sinkhorn iterations
sinkhorn_iterations.description: Row and column normalisation passes of the assignment.

native.produces: A feature vector for each input from an encoder trained without labels so that the prototype assignment computed for one distorted copy of the input can be predicted from a second distorted copy, with the assignments forced to share the batch equally among the prototypes.
native.targetVariable: Nothing in the market: the training target is the soft assignment to learned prototypes that the other distorted copy of the same input received.
native.objectiveNote: This model's puzzle is a swapped cross-entropy between prototype codes, where the codes come from a Sinkhorn step that makes every prototype take an equal share of each batch, which is what stops all inputs from choosing one prototype.

metrics.why: Predicting one view's prototype code from the other view says nothing about the market, so the encoder is judged by freezing it and asking whether a single linear layer on its output can order up bars above down bars; this is the same number the Model Cycle reports for this model, so the native and the as-run primary are one quantity.
metrics.baseline: One half, the value of an ordering that carries no information, which is a mathematical constant.

metrics.why: It asks what the swapped-code training added by fitting the identical linear layer on the raw feature row and on the encoder before any prototype step, on the same folds.
metrics.baseline: The same linear layer on this model's raw input row and on its untrained encoder, on the same folds.

metrics.why: Each bar's nearest prototype is a by-product grouping, and if a new seed or the next fold reshuffles which bars share a prototype then the prototypes are an artefact of the equal-share rule and not market states.

The Sinkhorn step forces equal prototype shares inside a training batch, so the shares on unseen bars, where nothing is forced, show whether the prototypes are really all in use or whether a few absorb almost every bar.

If the equal-share step is too soft every input can send the same scores to all prototypes, the swapped loss still falls, and only a count of the independent directions the encoder output uses on unseen rows reveals it.
The swapped cross-entropy by epoch shows only that the two views' codes are becoming predictable from each other, which a degenerate set of prototypes also achieves, so it is never read as quality.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes an input price series, while this encoder outputs a feature vector per input and makes no claim about stationarity.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: This ratio belongs to fractional differencing of a price series; the prototype encoder differences nothing and has no such memory parameter.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: Although the method uses prototypes, their sizes are forced equal by the Sinkhorn step and no distance-based compactness is optimised, so this score would grade a property the model does not aim for.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: Explained variance grades a linear projection that rebuilds its input, and this encoder has no decoder and keeps no ordered components.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction Residual
notApplicable.why: Nothing is reconstructed: the encoder is trained to predict the other view's prototype code, not to rebuild the input it was shown.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette coefficient
notApplicable.why: The prototypes are made equal in size by the Sinkhorn step and not compact by a distance objective, so a tightness score would grade a property the method never optimises.

notApplicable.name: Held-out reconstruction error
notApplicable.why: The encoder has no decoder, and replacing a bar by its prototype is never used to rebuild the bar's features.

notApplicable.name: Expected calibration error
notApplicable.why: The embedding states no odds, and the linear layer used to read it is fitted with each class carrying half the loss, so its output sits around one half whatever the series' own up share is.

asRun.standInNote: The adapter pretrains the encoder and its prototypes on every finite bar of the training span with labels unread, using two distorted views of one bar's feature row in place of multi-crop images and no feature queue, with a Sinkhorn step that makes every prototype take an equal share of each batch; it then freezes the encoder and fits one linear layer on its output for the direction, so every as-run number measures that single-bar embedding plus the linear readout and not the specification's own representation tests.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the sigmoid of one linear layer on the standardised output of the frozen encoder for the bar's own feature row, with the prototypes discarded, fitted by full-batch Adam on a logistic loss in which each class carries half the weight plus a small weight penalty, with no calibration curve afterwards.

stepQuantity.unit: nats, with the pretext epochs holding the swapped cross-entropy between prototype codes and the probe epochs holding the class-weighted logistic loss

meaningful.why: The linear layer on the prototype-trained encoder's output was fitted with each class carrying half the loss, so this score, which weights up bars and down bars equally, is the proper score on the scale that readout was aiming at; its reference is the natural logarithm of two, the score of always saying one half.

It tests whether the embedding shaped by swapping Sinkhorn prototype codes between two views carries any ordering of up bars over down bars that one linear layer can read, independent of where the class weights centred the probability; it coincides with the native primary.
A bounded second look at the linear readout's probabilities on the prototype-trained encoder's output, read with the knowledge that they are centred on one half and not on the fold's up share.

The hard call cuts the readout's probability at one half, the point the class weights centred it on, so averaging the hit rate over up bars and down bars is the fair count of calls for this prototype-trained embedding.
One symmetric number for the up or down calls read from the prototype-trained encoder's output, which stays near zero if the linear layer learned to call a single side.

The share of correct calls from the linear readout on the prototype-trained embedding, to be read beside the majority-class accuracy of the same fold because the readout's cut reflects its even prior and not the series' up share.
It shows without bins whether the linear layer on the prototype-trained encoder's output spreads its probabilities too widely or too narrowly, which early stopping on few validation rows can cause.

It is what the sign of the linear readout on the prototype-trained embedding earned after costs when the engine went long at one half or above and short below, so it tests the direction call and nothing about the size of the probability.

The same direction calls from the readout on the prototype-trained encoder's output per unit of bar-to-bar swing in profit, under the engine's rule and costs; zero is an arithmetic marker and not a no-skill reference because a random caller pays costs.
The deepest fall of the account while following the readout's direction calls on the prototype-trained embedding, which describes the path of those calls under the engine's rule.
Winning trade dollars over losing trade dollars for trades opened and closed by flips of the linear readout on the prototype-trained encoder's output, after costs.
The share of closed trades that made money, where a trade lasts until the readout on the prototype-trained embedding flips side or the fold ends, so it reflects flips and not single predictions.
How often the linear readout on the prototype-trained encoder's output calls up, shown beside every trading number because a readout stuck on one side simply holds the market.

The forecast line comes from a second fit of the same adapter, a separately pretrained encoder with its own prototypes and a linear Huber layer on its output, so this tests that second embedding against forecasting no move on the same bars.
The typical miss in points of the Huber layer on the second prototype-trained encoder's output, to be read against the no-change forecast's miss on the same bars.

The share of forecasts from the Huber layer on the second prototype-trained encoder whose sign matched the move, counted only where both are non-zero after tick rounding; it is a different model from the one whose calls are traded.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The readout was told by its class weights to centre on one half, so the unweighted score charges it for the gap between that even prior and the fold's up share and not for what the prototype-trained embedding knows.
Calibration against the observed up share is biased by construction for a readout whose class weights centre it on one half.

The training curve holds the swapped cross-entropy between prototype codes and then a class-weighted logistic loss, while the validation curve holds the unweighted logarithmic loss, so their difference compares different quantities.
With long-only off and no stop or target the engine is always in the market once the readout has made a call, so this number describes the engine's rule.

caveats: The logged training loss changes meaning at the first probe epoch: the pretext epochs log the swapped cross-entropy between prototype codes with no validation score, and the probe epochs log the class-weighted logistic loss of the linear layer.

The equal-share rule makes every prototype take the same part of each batch, so rare market states are forced to share prototypes with common ones; the adapter logs the entropy of prototype usage per batch and the engine does not record it.
The model reads one bar's feature row and no window of earlier bars, and the prototypes are thrown away before the readout, so no prototype assignment reaches the scoreboard.
Only the linear layer is early-stopped on the validation rows; the encoder runs all of its pretext epochs and is never selected on any score.
The hyperparameter search moves only the pretext learning rate and the prototype count, and it scores trials by the trading objective on inner blocks of the training span and not by the swapped loss.
The price forecast is a second, separately pretrained copy of the model with a Huber layer, so the forecast line and the traded call do not come from one embedding.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks label_horizon_bars ahead, so any interval around these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.
For any root other than MNQ the cost per side is the MNQ account figure applied as a stated assumption.

masked_autoencoder.summary: Hides most patches of the recent-bar window; the encoder sees only the rest and a light decoder rebuilds what was hidden.
masked_autoencoder.implementationNote: Bridge: the pretext trains on every finite bar of the training span, labels unread; a linear probe on the frozen embedding gives P(up), a Huber head the price, both early-stopped on validation. Differs from the spec: patches are runs of bars in the causal window, not image patches; the mean of the encoder's tokens on the whole window is the embedding. Expect: near a plain logistic regression on the same features.

pretext_epochs.description: Passes over the training span's unlabelled bars with the self-supervised objective; no label is read.

head_epochs.label: Probe epochs
head_epochs.description: Epochs of the linear probe on the frozen embedding (25 full-batch steps each), stopped early on the validation rows.

patience.label: Patience
patience.description: Probe epochs without a better validation loss before the probe stops.

weight_decay.label: Weight decay
weight_decay.description: Shrinks the encoder's weights toward zero each pretext step.

batch_size.label: Batch size
batch_size.description: Bars per pretext step, drawn at random from the span (contrastive methods use the rest of the batch as negatives).

sequence_length.label: Sequence length
sequence_length.description: Bars in the causal window the encoder reads, ending at the bar predicted.

patch_bars.label: Patch bars
patch_bars.description: Bars per patch; each patch of the window is one token.

model_dimension.label: Model dimension
model_dimension.description: Width of every token; a multiple of the head count.

mask_ratio.label: Mask ratio
mask_ratio.description: Share of the patches hidden from the encoder.

decoder_dimension.label: Decoder dimension
decoder_dimension.description: Token width of the light decoder.

native.produces: The masked autoencoder outputs an encoder embedding of the input learned by rebuilding hidden patches from the visible ones, plus a rebuilt version of the hidden patches that is thrown away after pretraining.
native.targetVariable: the standardised values of the hidden patches of the input, predicted from the visible patches alone; no market outcome is read
native.objectiveNote: The puzzle is rebuilding patches: most patches are hidden, the encoder sees only the visible ones, a light decoder fills the gaps with mask tokens, and the squared error is counted on the hidden patches only against targets standardised patch by patch.

metrics.why: The literature grades a masked autoencoder by freezing the patch transformer and fitting a linear probe on its embedding, and the probe's ordering of up bars above down bars is exactly that grade here, so the native primary and the as-run number coincide and this record says so.
metrics.baseline: one half, the value of a probe whose score does not order the bars at all

metrics.why: The same linear probe is refitted on the raw standardised window of bars and on the patch transformer with untrained weights, and only the difference shows that hiding patches and rebuilding them taught the encoder anything a plain logistic regression on the same features lacks.
metrics.baseline: the same probe on the raw feature window and on the randomly initialised patch transformer, same folds

metrics.why: The squared error on hidden patches of windows the decoder never trained on, against per-patch standardised targets, checks that the visible runs of bars really let the model rebuild the hidden runs instead of replaying the training span.
metrics.baseline: predicting zero for every standardised patch value, which leaves the whole patch variance unexplained

metrics.why: The embedding is the mean of the patch tokens, and if those tokens all point the same way the probe has one direction to read no matter how low the patch rebuilding error fell, so the count of directions that carry variance is checked on unseen windows.
metrics.baseline: the embedding width set by model_dimension, the largest value the rank can take

metrics.why: The hidden-patch squared error per pretext epoch shows whether rebuilding converged at the chosen mask_ratio; it says the puzzle was learned, not that the embedding is useful for direction.

notApplicable.name: Wasserstein Distance
notApplicable.why: It grades generated samples against real ones, and this model produces an embedding and rebuilt hidden patches, not samples.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: It is a generator fidelity distance and the masked autoencoder's decoder is never used to draw new market rows.

notApplicable.name: Latent KL Divergence
notApplicable.why: There is no stochastic latent and no prior in a masked autoencoder, so no divergence term exists to report.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: It belongs to contrastive methods on a unit sphere; the collapse check that fits this encoder is the effective rank of its embedding.

notApplicable.name: Latent Kullback-Leibler divergence
notApplicable.why: The encoder is deterministic with no prior on its code, so there is no divergence term; that quantity belongs to the variational autoencoder.

notApplicable.name: Expected calibration error
notApplicable.why: Natively the model states no probability, and the class-balanced probe added on top is centred on one half by construction, so its gap to the observed up share is built in.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A patch-rebuilding encoder takes no position; any return figure measures the engine's trading rule applied to the probe, which is the as-run layer.

asRun.standInNote: The pretext is a real masked autoencoder, but its patches are runs of patch_bars consecutive bars in the causal window instead of image patches, the embedding is the mean of the patch tokens on the whole unmasked window, and the only thing scored is a linear probe on that frozen embedding, so every as-run number measures the patch encoder plus the probe and is expected to sit near a plain logistic regression on the same features.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the sigmoid of a linear probe on the frozen, standardised mean of the patch tokens, fitted by full-batch Adam with a logistic loss in which up bars and down bars each carry half the weight, with no calibration map afterwards.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar during the probe epochs; standardised squared error per hidden patch value during the pretext epochs

meaningful.why: The probe on the patch embedding was fitted with each class carrying half the loss, so the score that matches what it was asked to do is the logarithmic loss averaged over up bars and down bars separately, read against the natural logarithm of two.

It asks whether the mean of the patch tokens, read by one linear layer, orders up bars above down bars, which is the standard grade of a frozen pretrained encoder and does not depend on where the class-balanced probe centres its scale.
The probe's cut at one half sits on a fifty-fifty prior, so averaging the hit rate on up bars and on down bars is the hard-call number that matches how the patch embedding's probe was weighted.

It is the share of scored bars where the patch embedding's probe called the right side, read beside the training majority class because the cut reflects the probe's fitted fifty-fifty prior and not the up share of the series.
One symmetric number for the probe's four confusion cells, useful here because a probe on a weak patch embedding can drift into calling nearly every bar the same side.
It reads the same probe probability but also charges the gap between the probe's fifty-fifty centre and the real up share, so it is shown beside the class-balanced version and never alone.
A bounded score of the probe's probability on the patch embedding that a few confident misses cannot dominate, read with the same caveat that the probe is centred on one half.

The probe stops early on validation logarithmic loss with a light weight penalty, and the slope tells whether the spread of its log-odds on the patch embedding is too wide or too narrow regardless of the shifted centre.

If rebuilding hidden patches taught nothing about direction, the probe's weights stay near their zero start and every probability sits at one half; the spread of the probabilities shows that directly.
It is what trading the sign of the patch-embedding probe's call earned under the engine's rule after costs, read beside buy and hold on the same folds.
It relates the per-bar profit of following the patch-embedding probe's call to its variability under the engine's rule and costs; zero is an arithmetic marker here and not a no-skill level.
The deepest fall of the equity made by the probe's calls shows the path that came with the profit; it reflects the engine's always-in-the-market rule as much as the patch encoder.
Winning over losing trade money for the probe's call flips after costs; one is an arithmetic marker because a trader with random direction pays costs and lands below it.
The share of closed trades from the probe's call flips that ended above zero after costs, a trade-level view that only means something together with the average win and loss.

It grades a second fit of the same masked pretext whose embedding is read by a linear Huber probe on the scaled move, against forecasting no change on the same bars; it says nothing about the direction probe.
The size in points of the Huber probe's misses on the second patch encoder's embedding, read beside the no-change forecast error on the same resolved bars.
The share of the Huber probe's non-zero forecasts with the right sign; it is a separate readout from the traded call, which comes from the class-balanced direction probe.

One curve holds two quantities: the hidden-patch squared error for the first pretext_epochs steps, then the class-balanced logistic loss of the probe, so the jump at the first probe epoch is a change of quantity and not a training event.

The search over learning_rate and mask_ratio is scored by trading the probe's call on inner blocks of the training span, not by patch rebuilding error, and the best trial's score is optimistic by construction.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The probe's loss gives each class half the weight, so its probabilities are centred on one half and their gap to the observed up share is built in rather than a fault of the patch embedding.
It is the largest bin gap of the same binned comparison against the observed up share, which the class-balanced probe is not trying to match.
The overall lean it measures is the shift the class weighting puts in on purpose, so it reports the weighting and not a property of the encoder.
With long_only off and no stop or target set the engine never goes flat once in a trade, so this share of bars held describes the engine's rule and not the patch encoder.
The training value is the class-weighted loss with a weight penalty and the validation value is the unweighted logarithmic loss, two different quantities, so their difference is not an overfit gap.

caveats: The pretext reads every bar of the fold's training span with a finite window, labelled or not, and never a validation or test bar; the labels enter only at the probe.
The kept probe is the epoch with the lowest validation logarithmic loss, so that validation number is optimistic and only the test walk is out of sample.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks label_horizon_bars ahead, so any interval on these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance, never a binomial interval.
For roots other than MNQ the cost per side is the MNQ account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.
The window holds only whole patches, so when sequence_length is not a multiple of patch_bars the oldest bars of the window are not read.

masked_graph_modeling.summary: Treats the recent bars as a graph, hides some bars' features and some links, and learns to restore both.
masked_graph_modeling.implementationNote: Bridge: the pretext trains on every finite bar of the training span, labels unread; a linear probe on the frozen embedding gives P(up), a Huber head the price, both early-stopped on validation. Differs from the spec: nodes are the window's bars and edges the time chain plus nearest bars by cosine similarity; there is no multi-asset graph. Expect: near a plain logistic regression on the same features.

native.produces: Masked graph modeling outputs node and graph embeddings from a graph network trained to restore node features and links that were hidden, plus the restored features and link scores themselves.
native.targetVariable: the feature vectors of the hidden nodes and the presence or absence of the hidden links, predicted from the visible part of the same graph; no market outcome is read
native.objectiveNote: The puzzle has two parts added together: squared error on the features of masked nodes and binary cross-entropy on whether a removed link existed, so the encoder must learn both what a node looks like and who it is connected to.

metrics.why: Masked graph pretraining is graded in the literature by a linear classifier on the frozen node embeddings, and here that classifier's ordering of up bars above down bars is the same grade, so the native primary and the as-run number coincide and this record says so.
metrics.baseline: one half, the value of a probe whose score does not order the bars at all

metrics.why: The probe is refitted on the raw features of the last bar and on the graph convolutions with untrained weights, which separates what restoring masked nodes and links taught from what message passing over the similarity links gives for free.
metrics.baseline: the same probe on the raw features and on the randomly initialised graph encoder, same folds

metrics.why: The squared error on masked node features of graphs the model never trained on shows whether neighbours really carry enough to restore a hidden node; it covers the node half of the objective only, the link half has no registry metric.
metrics.baseline: predicting each feature's training mean for every hidden node, which leaves the whole feature variance unexplained

metrics.why: Repeated graph convolutions average each node with its neighbours and can smooth every node toward one vector, so the count of embedding directions that still carry variance on unseen graphs is the over-smoothing check.
metrics.baseline: the embedding width, twice hidden_size, the largest value the rank can take

metrics.why: The summed node and link loss per pretext epoch shows whether restoring converged at the chosen node_mask_ratio and edge_mask_ratio; it is a convergence trace of the puzzle and no score of direction.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test applies to a transformed price series and this model outputs embeddings of graph nodes, not a series.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: It is a fractional-differencing quantity and was stamped here by a generator; masked graph modeling does no differencing.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: The model produces no cluster assignment, so there are no groups whose tightness could be measured.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: It belongs to principal components; the graph encoder is nonlinear and its masked-node reconstruction share replaces it.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity augmented Dickey-Fuller p-value
notApplicable.why: It tests whether a single price series has a unit root, and nothing in restoring masked nodes and links produces or transforms a series to be tested.

notApplicable.name: Structure stability recurrence
notApplicable.why: It counts how often a learned edge, selected feature or matched component reappears across refits, and here the graph is an input rebuilt inside each window from that window's own bars by the time chain and by similarity, with no fitted links, so there is no learned object per fold whose recurrence could be counted.

notApplicable.name: Expected calibration error
notApplicable.why: Natively no probability of a market outcome is stated, and the class-balanced probe added on top is centred on one half by construction.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A network that restores hidden nodes and links takes no position; return figures measure the engine's trading rule applied to the probe.

head_epochs.label: Probe epochs

temperature.description: Softmax temperature of the contrastive (or prototype) scores; lower is sharper.

native.produces: A context vector for each position in a sequence, the running state of a recurrent network fed the encoded observations so far, learned so that it can pick the encodings that really came next out of a line-up of decoys.
native.targetVariable: Which encoded future observation truly follows the current context, among one true candidate and many decoys taken from other positions; no market label is read.
native.objectiveNote: The invented puzzle is a noise-contrastive classification: one linear map per step ahead scores every candidate future encoding against the context, and pushing the true one to the top raises a lower bound on the information the context shares with the future, a bound that can never exceed the natural logarithm of the number of candidates in the line-up.

metrics.why: The specification judges the context vector by fitting a linear classifier on it while the encoder stays frozen, and that score only means something as a difference: the identical linear classifier on the raw inputs, and on the context of the recurrent network before any future-picking training, shows how much the contrastive puzzle itself added.
metrics.baseline: The same linear classifier fitted on the standardised raw features of the same bars, and on the context vector of the same network with untrained weights.

metrics.why: The linear classifier read off the frozen recurrent context gives every bar a score, and this area says whether the bars it scores higher really are followed by the positive class more often, which is the linear evaluation the specification describes; in the Model Cycle the downstream class is the up move, so this native number and the as-run number are one and the same.
metrics.baseline: One half, the value when the ordering of bars by the classifier carries no information about the outcome on the same series.

metrics.why: The logged value is the noise-contrastive loss averaged over the steps ahead, so it shows only whether the context is learning to pick the true future window out of the batch; neighbouring bars can be matched from slow features such as the volatility level, so a low value proves the puzzle was solved and says nothing about direction.
metrics.baseline: The natural logarithm of the number of windows in a batch, which is the loss of picking the future window at random.

metrics.why: Decoys must be told apart, so the context rarely shrinks to a single point, yet it can still flatten into a few directions that merely track the time of day or the volatility level, and this rank counts how many independent directions of the context vector actually vary on unseen bars.
metrics.baseline: The width of the context vector, set by hidden_size, which is the largest value the rank can take.

metrics.why: The contrastive scores are divided by a temperature, and a small temperature makes the gradient through the recurrent context spike, so the size of the gradient before clipping shows whether the future-picking training ran smoothly or was being held back by the clip.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: The generator stamped a unit-root test of the input series on a method whose output is a learned context vector, so it never described this model.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: No fractional differencing happens anywhere in the encoder, the recurrent context or the future-scoring maps, so this ratio has nothing to measure.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: The contrastive puzzle separates a true future from decoys and never assigns bars to clusters, so cluster tightness was never defined for it.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: No eigenvalue decomposition is fitted; whether the context vector has collapsed is answered by the effective rank of the embedding instead.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction Residual
notApplicable.why: Nothing is rebuilt, because the whole point of the contrastive score is to avoid generating the future observation at all.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter trains the real future-picking pretext on every finite bar of the fold's training span with labels unread, taking future bars only from inside that span and using the other windows of the batch as decoys, then freezes the encoder and fits a linear probe on the recurrent context to give the probability of up; every as-run number therefore grades the context vector plus that probe on the direction label and none of them grades how well the future was picked.
asRun.probabilityNote: The last sequence_length bars are encoded bar by bar, a gated recurrent network summarises them into a context vector, that vector is standardised with training statistics, and the probability of up is the sigmoid of a single linear layer fitted by the probe's own class-balanced logistic likelihood, each class carrying half, with no calibration map afterwards.

stepQuantity.unit: the noise-contrastive pretext loss in nats during the pretext epochs with no validation value, then nats of class-weighted logistic loss for the probe epochs beside the plain validation logarithmic loss

meaningful.why: The probe on the recurrent context was fitted with up bars and down bars each carrying half the loss, so its odds are centred on an even prior and this balanced score is the proper one for them, read against the natural logarithm of two, the score of quoting one half on every bar.

The probe is one straight cut through the context vector, so the ordering of test bars it produces is the cleanest reading of whether the future-picking training put direction information where a linear readout can reach it, free of the even-prior centring.

It grades the same sigmoid of the linear readout on a bounded scale, and since the probe starts from zero weights and stops early its probabilities sit close to one half, so this score mostly shows whether the small tilts away from one half point the right way.

The epoch of the linear head was chosen on this plain score over the validation rows, and on test bars it charges the probe for being centred on an even prior, so it is shown for continuity with the validation curve and not as the headline.

A head that starts at zero and is stopped after a few epochs usually understates what the context vector knows, and a slope above one on test bars would show exactly that timid scaling without needing probability bins.

If the context vector carries nothing about direction the linear head stays near its zero start and every bar is quoted near one half, and this spread shows at a glance whether the probe ever committed.

The class-weighted probe treats up and down as equally likely, so the fair hit rate for its hard call is the average of the share of up bars caught and the share of down bars caught, read against one half.

It is the plain hit rate of calling up when the linear readout of the context is positive, read against the fold's majority class; because the probe is centred on an even prior the cut sits at that prior and not at the series' own up share.
It puts in one symmetric number whether the sign of the linear readout of the recurrent context moves with the actual direction, with zero meaning the calls carry nothing.

It is the money made by going long whenever the probe on the context vector reads above one half and short otherwise, under the engine's next-open fill and costs, read against buy and hold on the same folds and beside the trade count.

It measures how steadily the sign of the probe's readout earned money per bar after costs; a readout that hovers at one half flips often and pays a round trip each time, which this ratio shows before any profit figure does.
It is the deepest hole the account fell into while following the context probe's call bar after bar, the price paid for whatever those calls earned.

It compares what the winning trades opened by a flip of the probe's call earned with what the losing ones gave back after costs, and is unstable when the probe flips only a few times, so it is read with the trade count.

It counts the share of closed trades that ended in profit, where a trade ends when the context probe changes its call, so it describes the calls under the engine's exit rule and is read with the predicted up share.

The forecast comes from a second fit of the same adapter, its own future-picking encoder with a linear head trained by Huber loss on the scaled move, so this skill tests whether a context vector says anything about the size and sign of the move against forecasting no change.
It is the size in points of the miss of that second encoder's linear forecast, which starts at the median training move and is stopped early, so it is read beside the error of forecasting no move.
It tests the sign of the second encoder's forecast, a different network and head from the probe that makes the traded call, so the two direction hit rates need not agree.

During the pretext epochs the curve is the future-picking loss, read against the natural logarithm of the batch size, and from the first probe epoch it becomes the class-weighted logistic loss of the linear head, so the jump between the two is a change of quantity and not a learning event.
It is reported only for the pretext epochs, where a spike before clipping shows the temperature-scaled contrast pulling the recurrent context too hard; the probe epochs report none.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The probe's odds are centred on an even prior by its class weighting, so their gap from the series' own up share is built in and says nothing about the context vector.

The training curve holds the pretext loss and then a class-weighted loss with a weight penalty, while the validation curve holds the plain logarithmic loss, so their difference compares two different quantities.
With both directions allowed and no stop or target the engine is always in a position once the probe has made its first call, so the share describes the engine's rule and not the model.

caveats: The future bars the pretext must pick out are taken only from inside the fold's training span, so no validation or test bar is ever a target or a decoy.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because each label looks label_horizon_bars ahead, so any interval around these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.

The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

native.produces: A latent state for each observation together with the model's own prediction of what comes next, so the leftover prediction error, the surprise, is available at every step and at every level of the hierarchy.
native.targetVariable: The next observation, or the next latent state, of the same sequence given the context so far; no market label is read.
native.objectiveNote: The invented puzzle is generative where contrastive methods are discriminative: the model must actually produce the coming observation or latent and is charged the squared miss or the negative log-likelihood, which the specification ties to minimising surprise, so nothing in the loss compares the truth with decoys; the next-latent predictor takes no action as input, because the market does not react to the model, and it predicts latents, never prices.

metrics.why: The specification reads the learned latents with a linear classifier on frozen weights, and the honest form of that test is a difference: the same linear classifier on the raw inputs, and on the latents of the network before any error-minimising training, shows whether learning to anticipate the next step produced features worth having.
metrics.baseline: The same linear classifier fitted on the standardised raw features of the same bars, and on the latent of the same network with untrained weights.

metrics.why: The linear classifier on the frozen latent and its surprise gives each bar a score, and this area says whether higher-scored bars really are followed by the positive class more often; in the Model Cycle that class is the up move, so the native linear-evaluation number and the as-run number are the same number.
metrics.baseline: One half, the value when the ordering of bars by the classifier carries no information about the outcome on the same series.

metrics.why: Minimising the miss between the predicted and the actual next latent is the whole training signal, so the same miss on unseen bars, measured in latent units for each step ahead, shows whether the top-down prediction learned the rhythm of the series or only memorised the training span.
metrics.baseline: The error of predicting that the next latent equals the current latent on the same unseen bars.

metrics.why: The cheapest way to make the next latent predictable is to make every latent the same, so this rank counts how many independent directions of the latent state still vary on unseen bars and catches a hierarchy that predicts perfectly because it says nothing.
metrics.baseline: The width of the latent state, set by latent_dimension, which is the largest value the rank can take.

metrics.why: The logged value is the miss between each predicted and each actual next latent or observation, charged as a squared error or as a negative log-likelihood, so the curve shows whether the top-down prediction is settling; its level depends on the scale of the latents and is never a score of the representation.
