metrics.why: The specification reads the transformer's frozen features with a linear classifier, and that tests the pretraining only as a difference: the same linear classifier on the raw inputs, on the transformer before any pretext training, and with each pretext task switched off in turn shows which puzzle, if any, earned its place.
metrics.baseline: The same linear classifier fitted on the standardised raw features of the same bars, and on the summary representation of the same transformer with untrained weights.

metrics.why: The linear classifier on the frozen summary representation gives each sequence a score, and this area says whether higher-scored sequences really belong to the positive class more often; in the Model Cycle that class is the up move, so the native linear-evaluation number and the as-run number are the same number.
metrics.baseline: One half, the value when the ordering of bars by the classifier carries no information about the outcome on the same series.

metrics.why: For the masked modelling task the transformer must fill in tokens it cannot see from the ones it can, so the miss on hidden tokens of unseen sequences, as a share of their variance, shows whether self-attention learned how neighbouring stretches of the series constrain each other.
metrics.baseline: One, the share obtained by filling every hidden token with the training mean of each feature.

metrics.why: The view-matching and teacher-following tasks can both be satisfied by a summary representation that is the same for every sequence, so this rank counts how many independent directions of the summary still vary on unseen sequences.
metrics.baseline: The width of the summary representation, set by model_dimension, which is the largest value the rank can take.

metrics.why: Self-attention is the reason for choosing a transformer, and the spread of each attention head over the tokens shows whether the encoder looks across the whole sequence or stares at the latest token, which helps explain a result and never grades it.
metrics.baseline: The natural logarithm of the number of tokens, the entropy of a head that looks at every token equally.

metrics.why: When several pretext tasks are summed the total loss hides which one is moving, so the curve is read per term, reconstruction, view contrast and teacher distance, and only as evidence that each puzzle is being worked on.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: The generator stamped a unit-root test of the input series on a family of transformer pretext tasks, so it never applied.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: No fractional differencing takes place in the token embedding, the attention layers or the pretext heads.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: The transformer produces representations and rebuilt tokens, never cluster assignments, so cluster cohesion was never defined.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: It belongs to principal components, and the attention encoder is non-linear with no eigenvalues to accumulate.

notApplicable.name: Expected calibration error
notApplicable.why: Natively the encoder states no probability of an outcome, only representations and rebuilt tokens, so there are no stated odds to check.

asRun.standInNote: Where the specification lists alternative pretext tasks, the runnable adapter trains one patch transformer on three of them at once, with tokens that are runs of patch_bars bars inside the causal window: rebuild hidden patches, match the summary tokens of two jittered and masked views, and follow a momentum teacher, on every finite bar of the fold's training span with labels unread; the encoder is then frozen and a linear probe on its summary token gives the probability of up, so every as-run number grades that summary token plus the probe on the direction label and none grades the reconstruction, the contrast or the distillation.
asRun.probabilityNote: The last sequence_length bars are cut into patches of patch_bars bars, self-attention blocks mix the patch tokens with a summary token, the summary token's output is standardised with training statistics, and the probability of up is the sigmoid of a single linear layer fitted by the probe's own class-balanced logistic likelihood, each class carrying half; no mask is applied at prediction time and no calibration map follows.

stepQuantity.unit: the weighted sum of masked-patch squared error, view-contrast loss in nats and cosine distance to the teacher during the pretext epochs with no validation value, then nats of class-weighted logistic loss for the probe epochs beside the plain validation logarithmic loss

meaningful.why: The probe on the transformer's summary token was fitted with up bars and down bars each carrying half the loss, so its odds are centred on an even prior and this balanced score is the proper one for them, read against the natural logarithm of two, the score of quoting one half on every bar.

The probe is one straight cut through the summary token, so the ordering of test bars it produces is the cleanest reading of whether three label-free tasks on patches of bars left direction information where a linear readout can reach it, free of the even-prior centring.

It grades the same sigmoid of the linear readout on a bounded scale, and since the head starts from zero weights and stops early its probabilities sit close to one half, so this score mostly shows whether the small tilts the summary token allows point the right way.

The epoch of the linear head was chosen on this plain score over the validation rows, and on test bars it charges the probe for being centred on an even prior, so it is shown for continuity with the validation curve and not as the headline.

A head that starts at zero and is stopped after a few epochs usually understates what the summary token knows, and a slope above one on test bars would show exactly that timid scaling without needing probability bins.

If the summary token carries nothing about direction, or the view-matching task flattened it, the linear head stays near its zero start and every bar is quoted near one half, and this spread shows at a glance whether the probe ever committed.

The class-weighted probe treats up and down as equally likely, so the fair hit rate for its hard call on the transformer's summary token is the average of the share of up bars caught and the share of down bars caught, read against one half.

It is the plain hit rate of calling up when the linear readout of the summary token is positive, read against the fold's majority class; because the probe is centred on an even prior the cut sits at that prior and not at the series' own up share.
It puts in one symmetric number whether the sign of the linear readout of the transformer's summary token moves with the actual direction, with zero meaning the calls carry nothing.

It is the money made by going long whenever the probe on the summary token reads above one half and short otherwise, under the engine's next-open fill and costs, read against buy and hold on the same folds and beside the trade count.

It measures how steadily the sign of the probe's readout earned money per bar after costs; the window slides one bar at a time while the patches are several bars wide, so the summary token can shift as bars cross patch borders and flip the call, and each flip pays a round trip that this ratio shows first.
It is the deepest hole the account fell into while following the summary-token probe's call bar after bar, the price paid for whatever those calls earned.

It compares what the winning trades opened by a flip of the probe's call earned with what the losing ones gave back after costs, and is unstable when the probe flips only a few times, so it is read with the trade count.

It counts the share of closed trades that ended in profit, where a trade ends when the probe on the summary token changes its call, so it describes the calls under the engine's exit rule and is read with the predicted up share.

The forecast comes from a second fit of the same adapter, its own patch transformer with a linear head trained by Huber loss on the scaled move, so this skill tests whether a summary token says anything about the size and sign of the move against forecasting no change.

It is the size in points of the miss of that second transformer's linear forecast, which starts at the median training move and is stopped early, so it is read beside the error of forecasting no move.
It tests the sign of the second transformer's forecast, a different network and head from the probe that makes the traded call, so the two direction hit rates need not agree.

During the pretext epochs the curve is the weighted sum of the patch reconstruction, view contrast and teacher distance, each also written separately to the run log, and from the first probe epoch it becomes the class-weighted logistic loss of the linear head, so the jump between the two is a change of quantity and not a learning event.
It is reported only for the pretext epochs, where a spike before clipping shows the three tasks pulling the attention layers in different directions; the probe epochs report none.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The probe's odds are centred on an even prior by its class weighting, so their gap from the series' own up share is built in and says nothing about the summary token.

The training curve holds a sum of three pretext losses and then a class-weighted loss with a weight penalty, while the validation curve holds the plain logarithmic loss, so their difference compares two different quantities.
With both directions allowed and no stop or target the engine is always in a position once the probe has made its first call, so the share describes the engine's rule and not the model.

caveats: The three pretext losses are written separately to the run log so a rerun with one weight set to zero can show which task carries the probe, but no such ablation is run or stored by the engine.
Attention weights of the patch transformer are not recorded, so the scoreboard cannot say which stretch of the window the summary token relies on.

The encoder kept is the one from the last pretext epoch with no selection, and only the linear head's epoch is chosen on the validation rows, so the validation logarithmic loss is optimistic for the head.

The hyperparameter search over learning_rate and mask_ratio maximises the simulator's Sharpe ratio on inner blocks of the training span, not the pretext loss and not the probe's loss, and its best score is optimistic by construction.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because each label looks label_horizon_bars ahead, so any interval around these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than MNQ the cost per side is the MNQ account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.
